message.content:
Yes—you can file a noise complaint with the City of Atlanta’s local authorities.  
In Atlanta, noise violations are generally handled by the **City of Atlanta Police Department** (via the Code Enforcement Division) or the **Department of Public Safety**. Here’s how you can do it:

| Step | What to Do | Where/How |
|------|------------|-----------|
| 1 | Gather details | Note the exact address, time(s), and nature of the noise (e.g., loud music, construction, barking dogs). |
| 2 | Call 311 | Dial **311** from any phone in Atlanta (or 911 if it’s an emergency). The dispatcher will route your call to the appropriate department. |
| 3 | Use the online portal | Visit the City of Atlanta’s official website and navigate to the “Noise Complaint” section under the **Code Enforcement** or **Public Safety** pages. You’ll find a form to fill out online. |
| 4 | Submit the complaint | Provide all required information, attach any evidence (photos, audio recordings, witness statements), and submit. |
| 5 | Follow up | After filing, you’ll receive a reference number. You can track the status via the online portal or by calling 311 again. |

### Quick Links
- **City of Atlanta 311**: https://www.atlantaga.gov/311 (online chat, phone, or mobile app)
- **Noise Complaint Form**: https://www.atlantaga.gov/CodeEnforcement/NoiseComplaint (direct link may change; search “noise complaint” on the site)
- **Atlanta Police Department – Code Enforcement**: https://www.atlantaga.gov/Police/CodeEnforcement

### Tips
- **Time matters**: Noise ordinances often specify quiet hours (e.g., 10 p.m.–7 a.m.). Be sure to note when the disturbance occurs.
- **Evidence helps**: If possible, record the noise or take photos of the source. This can speed up the investigation.
- **Multiple complaints**: If the same issue persists, you can file additional complaints. The city keeps a log of repeated violations.

If you’re unsure which department to contact, start with 311—they’ll direct you to the correct office. Good luck!
